campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 15, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered updates to the city's theater use policy, a cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose for resurfacing work worth up to $335,000, and the annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27. The Council also considered a budget adjustment to fund replacement equipment.
keyTopics: Proposed modifications to Council Policy Section 14 (Theater Use Policy)
Cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose for resurfacing, not to exceed $335,000
Annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27
Budget adjustment to fund replacement equipment

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 16, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up routine business including meeting minutes, vendor payment approvals, and a conflict of interest code update, along with final map approvals for two residential lot splits. The Council also considered two appeals of Planning Commission decisions on residential projects, and discussed law enforcement service options ahead of upcoming community town hall meetings.
keyTopics: Final map approvals for lot splits at 20517 Carniel Avenue and 19351 Saratoga Los Gatos Road
Appeal of Planning Commission approval for a single-family home and ADU at 14650 6th Street
Appeal of Planning Commission approval of a three-lot subdivision at 14486 Oak Place
Law enforcement service options for Saratoga, ahead of September 19 and 30 town hall meetings
Resolution amending the City's Conflict of Interest Code

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 22, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council took up a routine wastewater treatment agreement, a transportation board reappointment, new appointments to city commissions, and an amended legal services contract. Council also considered an interim urgency ordinance placing a temporary moratorium on detention and custodial facility applications in the city.
keyTopics: Interim urgency ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on applications for detention or custodial facilities
Addendum No. 14 to the Regional Water Quality Control Plant agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View
Reappointment of Councilmember Jonathan Weinberg to the VTA Board representing north counties
Appointments to the Complete Streets, Environmental, and Planning Commissions
Amendment to the legal services agreement with Berliner Cohen, LLP, updating the monthly retainer and hourly rate

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 15, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine business, including approval of minutes from prior meetings and the town's monthly financial and investment report for July 2026. The Council also considered several service and professional services agreements, including amendments related to heating, ventilation, and air conditioning work and other professional services contracts.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the September 1, 2026 Closed Session and regular Town Council meetings
Monthly Financial and Investment Report for July 2026 (with a correction)
A second amendment to an existing agreement
A first amendment to an agreement for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning services
New agreements for professional services with outside contractors

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 23, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed the upcoming City Council agendas for September 29 and October 6, 2026, including whether any items needed new additions or scheduled 'time certain' slots. The committee also considered the public record log, a mayoral travel request, and a proposal to fund a District 1 community group's participation in a statewide local government association.
keyTopics: Review and possible additions to the September 29, 2026 final Council agenda
Review and possible additions to the October 6, 2026 draft Council agenda
Public record log covering September 10-17, 2026
Mayor's request to travel
District 1 San Jose Sharks Community Funds approval for the California Association of Local Agency Formation Commissions

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — September 22, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met in closed session to discuss potential litigation involving fire truck manufacturers and to consider the appointment of a City Attorney, followed by a regular session covering a range of items including field renovations at Shoreline Park, a solar and battery storage energy project, updates to historic preservation rules, and pay adjustments for top city officials. Residents also had the chance to speak on issues not on the agenda.
keyTopics: Potential legal case involving fire apparatus manufacturers (Golden State Fire Apparatus, Pierce, Oshkosh, REV Group, Rosenbauer, FAMA)
Appointment of a new City Attorney
Professional services agreement for Shoreline Athletic Fields renovation project
Solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage project actions
Historic Preservation Ordinance and zoning map update, and Active Transportation Plan adoption

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — September 19, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: This was a special morning session of the Sunnyvale City Council held for the annual 'State of the City' event. The agenda covered logistics for the event rather than typical policy or budget business.
keyTopics: State of the City special session
Event schedule for the gathering

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 15, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met on September 15, 2026, starting with closed-session discussions on potential litigation and a real property negotiation involving land at 10480 Finch Avenue with the Cupertino Union School District. The public meeting included recognition of Cupertino High School students for their achievements at a national business leadership conference, followed by a consent calendar covering routine business items like meeting minutes, bill payments, an audit committee ordinance, and a new AI use policy for the Council.
keyTopics: Closed-session discussion on potential litigation and real property negotiations (price/terms) for 10480 Finch Avenue with the Cupertino Union School District
Recognition of Cupertino High School students for achievements at the 2026 FBLA National Leadership Conference
Postponement of an ordinance updating building code definitions for "attic," "garages," and "square footage" to October 6, 2026
Adoption of a new Artificial Intelligence (AI) City Council Policy

Appointment of Mayor Kitty Moore and Councilmember Ray Wang to a subcommittee evaluating City Lobbyist proposals for 2027-2028, plus a response to the county Civil Grand Jury's pothole-damage claims report

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — September 22, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council considered a major housing proposal at 451-475 El Camino Real, involving a prezone, a General Plan land use pre-designation, an annexation application, and a vesting tentative subdivision map to allow 408 residential units plus related site improvements. An Environmental Impact Report prepared under CEQA was part of the review. The Council also met in closed session to discuss existing and anticipated litigation matters.
keyTopics: Proposal to annex and prezone 451-475 El Camino Real for a 408-unit residential development with on- and off-site improvements
Review of an Environmental Impact Report (EIR) prepared under CEQA for the project
Vesting tentative subdivision map application tied to the development
Closed session on existing litigation: City of Santa Clara/Silicon Valley Power and Northern California Power Agency v. California Department of Water Resources
Closed session on anticipated litigation matters

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council reviewed a draft plan for spending federal Community Development Block Grant funds and got updates on the red light camera traffic safety program and the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The Council also considered bond-related actions tied to the former Redevelopment Agency's successor agency.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution actions for the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency, including sale and issuance of refunding bonds

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — September 22, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto City Council received routine liaison and department updates, then turned to two park-related items: proposed guidelines for using synthetic turf on playgrounds, and a recommendation on park improvement rules for the Foothills Nature Preserve Improvement Project.
keyTopics: Proposed guidelines for synthetic turf use on playgrounds
Park Improvements Ordinance recommendation for the Foothills Nature Preserve Improvement Project
Ad hoc committee and council liaison updates
Department staff presentation
